course_name_en: Measurement, Control and Regulation Technology II (MSR2)

learning_outcomes.text: Students possess basic knowledge for automation projects on products and processes.
Knowledge in the area of system description of measuring transducers and sensors for different measured variables in measurement technology.
Knowledge of the methodology for the practice-oriented design of industrial control systems in control technology.
With this basic knowledge, students are able to familiarize themselves with more complex automation projects and systems.
Students are able to organize themselves into teams in a division of labor to conduct practical experiments.
Students are able to apply personal competencies for communication, problem-solving, and decision-making.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to measurement technology in mechanical engineering
Structures of wiring of measuring devices
Dynamic and static properties of transmission elements of the measuring chain
System description of measuring transducers and sensors for different measured variables: force, mass, pressure, acceleration, velocity, length and angle, temperature, flow
Logic networks and switching functions, elementary operations, basic functions
Postulates and laws of Boolean algebra
Normal forms of switching function, function tables, Karnaugh-Veitch diagrams
Advantages of circuit minimization, transformation of switching functions
Pneumatic control systems, semiconductor control systems
Genesis of memory behavior, elementary memory, timing elements
State description and design, state graph, function diagram
Representation, examples in different implementation forms
Understanding and implementing simple experimental setups; logging and evaluating measurements
Exercising appropriate communication skills, compiling and presenting work results
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded for a passed written exam (grade). Active participation in the practical training is a prerequisite for taking the exam.
